cues.text: Uranus kept turning up in the wrong part of the sky.
What if another planet was pulling it off its expected path?
In 1846, French mathematician Urbain Le Verrier used those differences
to predict where the unseen planet might be.
He sent his calculation to an observatory in Berlin.
The night the letter arrived, Johann Galle and Heinrich d’Arrest compared
their telescope view with a star chart.
A point of light was missing from the chart, about one degree from
where Le Verrier had told them to look.
By the next night it had shifted against the stars.
